label: Population (GHSL, primary)
native_grain: 30 arc-second raster (about 0.93 km at the equator), WGS84; JRC's own resampling of the 100 m / 1 km Mollweide product
lineage: Read the 30 arc-second raster over the window (+0.1° pad) > Assign each pixel to the H3 res-6 cell containing the pixel centre > Sum pixel populations per cell
caveat: Modelled residential population for 2020. Not a count. Pixel-centre assignment means cells on the edge of a dense town can gain or lose a few hundred people relative to an exact area-weighted split.

label: Population (WorldPop, secondary)
lineage: Read the 30 arc-second raster over the window (+0.1° pad) > Assign each pixel to the H3 res-6 cell containing the pixel centre > Sum pixel populations per cell
caveat: Constrained product: people are placed only where settlement is mapped, so many rural cells are empty here but not in GHSL. National totals are adjusted to UN estimates.

label: Population disagreement D, signed (WorldPop vs GHSL)
lineage: Take pop.ghsl (G) and pop.worldpop (W) for the cell > Skip cells where both are below 100 people > D = 100 x (W - G) / ((W + G) / 2)
caveat: Signed: positive means WorldPop places more people here than GHSL, negative fewer. It shows how far two reputable models disagree, not which is right. Its magnitude |D| and the difference in people are separate layers with different meanings.

label: Population disagreement magnitude |D|
lineage: Take D from pop.disagreement > |D| = absolute value of D (the sign is dropped)
caveat: How large the disagreement is, whatever its direction. A different analytical object from D: it cannot say which model is higher. The inspector shows the signed D beside it.

label: Population difference in people, signed (WorldPop minus GHSL)
lineage: Take pop.ghsl (G) and pop.worldpop (W) for the cell > Difference = W - G, in people (signed)
caveat: Signed difference in people. Large differences in people sit in dense places even when D is small; large D can sit where few people live. Read it beside D.

label: Water share of cell surface (GHS-SMOD)
native_grain: 30 arc-second raster (about 0.93 km), WGS84; JRC's resampling of the native 1 km Mollweide grid
lineage: Read the 30 arc-second raster over the window (+0.1° pad) > Assign each pixel to the H3 res-6 cell containing the pixel centre > Share of pixels in the cell classed 10 (water) by GHS-SMOD
caveat: Physical surface, recorded independently of country outlines and of population. A cell can be water and inside a country, or land and outside every outline.

label: Urban population share (GHS-SMOD)
native_grain: 30 arc-second raster (about 0.93 km), WGS84; JRC's resampling of the native 1 km Mollweide grid
lineage: Read the 30 arc-second raster over the window (+0.1° pad) > Assign each pixel to the H3 res-6 cell containing the pixel centre > Weight each pixel by its GHS-POP 2020 population (same grid) > Urban share = population in urban centres (class 30) + urban clusters (21-23), over all non-water population
caveat: Degree of Urbanisation classes are a harmonised international definition, not national definitions of 'urban'. The inspector shows the urban centre / urban cluster / rural split.

label: Travel time to nearest health facility, motorised
lineage: Request the 30 arc-second WCS subset for the window (+0.5° pad) > Assign each pixel to the H3 res-6 cell containing the pixel centre > Weight each pixel by GHS-POP 2020 sampled at the pixel centre (nearest pixel) > Population-weighted mean per cell; unweighted mean where nobody lives
caveat: Modelled best-case travel time assuming motorised transport is available. Says nothing about facility quality, staffing, cost or opening hours. The inspector shows the within-cell minimum and maximum, which is spread, not uncertainty.

label: Travel time to nearest health facility, walking only
lineage: Request the 30 arc-second WCS subset for the window (+0.5° pad) > Assign each pixel to the H3 res-6 cell containing the pixel centre > Weight each pixel by GHS-POP 2020 sampled at the pixel centre (nearest pixel) > Population-weighted mean per cell; unweighted mean where nobody lives
caveat: Modelled walking time with no vehicle. Same facility list and caveats as the motorised layer.

label: Years since the last population census
lineage: Transcribe the most recent completed census per country from the UNSD page > Years since = 2026 - census year > Attach to every cell that a country's geoBoundaries outline covers (at least 1% of the cell) > A cell covered by two or more outlines shows the country covering most of it; the inspector lists the others
caveat: A national fact spread over every cell, so it is the same for a capital and a remote valley. It matters because every population model above is anchored to these censuses.
